about: The four situations the plan's N10 row names (counterevidence, repeated failed attempts, missing inputs, stopping) and the one boundary around stopping, as inputs to the next-action decision. Each case is the progress snapshot `autopilotProgress.mjs` builds plus the agenda's own fields; `expect` lists the decisions that are right (any one passes), the model's wording is not judged. They are written situations, not production incidents: the first live runs on the deployment are what turn real ones into cases. The last four (N11, plan §11.3) are what a researcher's own words and files do to the decision: material added after a needs_input stop, a correction of the denominator, a message that only asks to pause, and one that only uses the word while redirecting the work. They carry `trigger` and `note` (the request the decision answers) and `pauseAllowed`, and their progress carries `researcherNotes`, `materials` and `lastStop` as `autopilotProgress.mjs` builds them.

cases.why: An independent check refuted the only gated claim. Running another evidence-update to re-prove it is the failure; a new direction or new literature is the change the plan asks for. Stopping is wrong: the question is open.

agenda.title: SGLT2 抑制剂与心衰住院
agenda.prompt: Does adding an SGLT2 inhibitor reduce all-cause mortality in HFpEF patients over 75? Track what the evidence supports and what is still unexplained.

claims.statement: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce all-cause mortality in HFpEF patients aged 75 and over.

cases.why: The last episode did not run (a dead runtime) and the one before found a gated, unchecked claim. Reading the failure as 'nothing found' and stopping, or abandoning the direction, is the failure the plan names: execution failure is never evidence.

agenda.title: 替尔泊肽头对头证据
agenda.prompt: Follow direct head-to-head evidence of tirzepatide versus semaglutide on weight and glycaemic control; do not substitute indirect comparisons.

claims.statement: In SURMOUNT-5, tirzepatide produced a larger mean weight reduction than semaglutide at 72 weeks.

cases.why: The question needs the researcher's own cohort, and the only episode so far found no dataset to analyse. Running data-prospecting again repeats a step that cannot succeed without the researcher; saying what is needed (needs_input), or turning to what published evidence can add, is the appropriate change.

agenda.title: 本院心衰注册研究
agenda.prompt: Analyse our hospital's heart-failure registry for the association between early SGLT2 inhibitor use and 90-day readmission. The registry export has not been shared yet.

cases.why: A narrow, one-off question that three completed episodes have answered, every claim gated and independently checked or reproduced. Another episode adds cost and no conclusion; stopping is a useful outcome.

agenda.title: 二甲双胍与维生素 B12
agenda.prompt: Is long-term metformin use associated with vitamin B12 deficiency? This is a one-off question; I only need a supported answer with its limits.

claims.statement: Long-term metformin use is associated with lower serum B12 in randomized and observational studies.
The association is dose- and duration-dependent; routine B12 monitoring is recommended by guidelines for long-term users.

cases.why: The same answered question, but the researcher has just started the agenda, so a stop is not allowed. The decision must run something; an answer that stops anyway is dropped by code and the rotation runs, which this case counts as a miss.

agenda.title: SGLT2 抑制剂与老年心衰
agenda.prompt: Does adding an SGLT2 inhibitor reduce all-cause mortality in HFpEF patients over 75? Use the cohort I hold where it is relevant.

lastStop.reason: 需要这批受试者的年龄分布数据，才能判断 75 岁以上亚组的结论能否适用于研究者的人群。

claims.statement: 在意向治疗人群中，SGLT2 抑制剂降低 HFpEF 患者全因死亡率。

cases.why: The researcher wrote that the denominator was wrong: the earlier finding was read in the intention-to-treat population and they need the randomised one, and that finding is the one still standing in the history. Stopping (the question is not answered) and an unrelated new direction both ignore the correction; re-checking the evidence on the corrected denominator is the change.
